name: spartadoc
description: Redact personal information from a document before your AI reads it: names, addresses and numbers are removed, you review them, and only the redacted version reaches the conversation.

interface.longDescription:
Spartadoc lets ChatGPT read a document that contains personal information without the original ever being attached to the conversation. It is built for professionals who handle their clients' documents: lawyers, notaries, accountants, financial planners, real estate brokers and others.

Ask ChatGPT to read a contract, a notarial deed, a will, financial statements, an investment statement or a purchase offer. A Spartadoc card appears in the chat with an upload button, the time left and the status. On the upload page you photograph or choose the document, and Spartadoc detects names, addresses, numbers, email addresses and phone numbers and masks them. You review every masked area, add or remove areas as needed, then tap "Send to my chat". Nothing reaches ChatGPT before you confirm.

The card then tells ChatGPT on its own that the document is sent: no need to come back and type anything. ChatGPT receives only the redacted version: the text in which each removed value is replaced by a label such as [PERSON_1], images of the redacted pages and a link to the redacted PDF. The original is deleted as soon as the redacted version is ready, and the redacted version is deleted 15 minutes after you send it. You can cancel an upload at any time.

Settings: the language of the upload page and labels (automatic, French or English), and automatic reading once the document is sent.

Works in French and English: documents in either language, and the upload page and the messages follow your language.

Requires a Spartadoc account with redaction enabled for your organization; when you connect, you sign in to your Spartadoc workspace. Automatic detection is an aid: you review and confirm what is sent.

En français :

Spartadoc permet à ChatGPT de lire un document qui contient des renseignements personnels sans que l’original soit jamais joint à la discussion. Il est pensé pour les professionnels qui manipulent les documents de leurs clients : avocats, notaires, comptables, planificateurs financiers, courtiers immobiliers et autres.

Demandez à ChatGPT de lire un contrat, un acte notarié, un testament, des états financiers, un relevé de placements ou une promesse d’achat. Une carte Spartadoc apparaît dans la discussion avec un bouton de dépôt, le temps restant et l’état. Sur la page de dépôt, vous photographiez ou choisissez le document ; Spartadoc y repère les noms, adresses, numéros, courriels et téléphones et les masque. Vous vérifiez chaque zone masquée, en ajoutez ou en retirez au besoin, puis touchez « Envoyer à ma discussion ». Rien ne parvient à ChatGPT avant votre confirmation.

La carte annonce alors elle-même l’envoi à ChatGPT : inutile de revenir écrire quoi que ce soit. ChatGPT ne reçoit que la version caviardée : le texte où chaque valeur retirée est remplacée par une étiquette comme [PERSONNE_1], l’image des pages caviardées et un lien vers le PDF caviardé. L’original est effacé dès que la version caviardée est prête, et celle-ci est effacée 15 minutes après votre envoi. Vous pouvez annuler un dépôt à tout moment.

Réglages : la langue de la page de dépôt et des étiquettes (automatique, français ou anglais), et la lecture automatique dès l’envoi.

Fonctionne en français et en anglais : des documents dans l’une ou l’autre langue, et la page de dépôt et les messages suivent votre langue.

Exige un compte Spartadoc dont l’organisation a activé le caviardage ; à la connexion, vous vous connectez à votre espace Spartadoc. La détection automatique est une aide : vous vérifiez et confirmez ce qui est envoyé.

publication.release_notes: 1.1.0: a Spartadoc card in the chat (upload button, time left, status, cancel) that tells ChatGPT on its own when the document is sent, so there is no need to come back and type "done"; plugin settings (language of the upload page and labels, automatic reading); a welcome after installation; tool titles in French and English; a "Back to ChatGPT" button at the end of the upload page.

positive.description: Opening an upload for a document that contains personal information
positive.prompt: I need you to read my purchase offer, but it has personal information in it. Can you redact it first?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls ouvrir_depot. A Spartadoc card appears under the call with an "Upload my document" button, the time left and the status; the reply also shows the upload link (https://<workspace>.spartadoc.com/c/<code>?lang=en&ia=chatgpt for an English conversation), valid for 15 minutes. The upload page opens in English. ChatGPT does not ask the user to attach the file to the chat.

positive.description: Reading the redacted document once the user has sent it from the upload page
positive.prompt: Done, I sent it. What does the document say?
positive.expected_behavior: After the reviewer taps the card's button (or the link from the previous case), uploads the sample document on the English page, reviews the masked areas and taps "Send to my chat", the Spartadoc card posts "Done, I sent it: please read the redacted document." in the chat on its own; typing the prompt above has the same effect. ChatGPT calls recuperer_document with no arguments (a read-only call on the latest upload: the upload is deleted on its own 15 minutes after it was sent). It receives the redacted text, in which each removed value is replaced by a label such as [PERSON_1] or [ADDRESS_1] (a French page gives [PERSONNE_1], [ADRESSE_1]), images of the redacted pages and a link to the redacted PDF. Its answer summarizes the document, keeps the labels as they are and never guesses the removed values. At the end of the upload page, a "Back to ChatGPT" button closes the page.

positive.description: Asking for the document before it has been sent
positive.expected_behavior: Asked right after an upload was opened but before the reviewer taps "Send to my chat": recuperer_document (read-only) reports that the document has not been sent yet (etat en_attente). ChatGPT asks the user to finish on the upload page; the card meanwhile shows "Upload your document" or, once a file is uploaded, "Document received".

positive.prompt: Actually, I changed my mind. Cancel that upload.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT may first ask the user to confirm, then calls annuler_depot with no arguments (it cancels the latest upload) and confirms that the upload is cancelled and its content deleted. The card then reads "Upload cancelled" (or "Link expired"), and opening the link shows that it has expired. The card's own "Cancel" button does the same after a second tap to confirm.

positive.description: Reading and changing the Spartadoc settings from the chat
positive.prompt: Show my Spartadoc settings, then set the upload page to French.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls lire_reglages (read-only) and lists the two settings: the language of the upload page and labels (auto, fr or en) and automatic reading once the document is sent (on by default). It then calls modifier_reglages with {"set": {"langue": "fr"}} and confirms the change. The next upload link carries lang=fr: the page opens in French and the labels are French ([PERSONNE_1]). The same two settings appear on the plugin's settings page.

negative.description: General question about real estate, no document involved
negative.prompt: What is a promise to purchase in Quebec real estate?
Write a short email to my client to schedule a house visit next Tuesday at 2 pm.
